Answer.signature: Answer(blocks: (Text | Callout | Code | Trace | Reveal | Flow | Table | Terms | Steps | Stat)[])
Answer.description: The root container: an ordered sequence of blocks that together explain the material.

Text.description: A short paragraph of plain prose. Use between visual blocks to carry the narrative.

Callout.description: The one thing the reader should not miss. tone 'insight' for the key idea, 'warning' for a pitfall or bug.

Code.signature: Code(title?: string, language?: string, code: string)
Code.description: A code block, quoted from the material or a minimal corrected/illustrative version of it. Keep it short — quote the lines that matter, not the whole file.

Trace.signature: Trace(title?: string, cells: string[], frames: {label: string, highlight?: number, compare?: number, verdict?: "keep" | "skip" | "note", vars?: {name: string, value: string}[]}[])
Trace.description: An interactive step-through of an algorithm or loop. Show the sequence being walked as cells, and one frame per meaningful step: which index is active, which it's compared against, the verdict, and the variables after the step. ALWAYS prefer this over Table for loops, recursion, and pointer algorithms.

Reveal.description: A prediction moment: pose a short question the student should answer in their head, hidden answer behind a click. Use once per explanation, at the point where guessing teaches the most — e.g. 'what does this return for [3,5,2]?'

Flow.description: A left-to-right chain of stages with arrows — for control flow, data flow, a pipeline, a lifecycle. 3 to 7 short node labels.

Table.description: A compact comparison or reference table. Use when the material contrasts things — options, cases, complexities. Max 5 columns.

Terms.description: Definitions for the jargon the material assumes. Only terms that actually appear in it.

Steps.description: An ordered walkthrough — what happens first, then, then. For tracing execution or a procedure in the notes.

Stat.signature: Stat(label: string, value: string, caption?: string)
Stat.description: One labelled figure the material states or directly implies — a complexity, a count, a limit. Never invent one.
